claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater plastic strain than commercially pure tungsten under the specified high-temperature loading.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has greater toughness than commercially pure tungsten under the specified high-temperature loading.
The chemically disordered multi-element matrix creates significant lattice distortions.
The lattice distortions impede dislocation pile-up.
The lattice distortions activate additional slip systems.
Refined grains and modified grain-boundary character facilitate plastic flow and energy absorption in WTaTiVZr.
Arc melting followed by homogenization produces a single-phase, chemically disordered BCC WTaTiVZr alloy.
Chemically induced lattice distortions modify grain-boundary characteristics.
Chemically induced lattice distortions reduce the Peierls barrier for dislocation motion.
Modified grain boundaries and lattice distortions promote secondary slip systems.
Atomic size-misfit and electronic effects disturb the regular lattice in WTaTiVZr.
Size-misfit and electronic effects reduce the local activation energy for dislocation motion.
Reduced local activation energy delays dislocation pile-up and permits additional slip systems to operate.
Enhanced dislocation motion and additional slip activity increase ductility and toughness relative to pure tungsten.
At approximately 1200°C, temperature-activated dislocation mechanisms are significant under the proposed strain rate.
Detrimental secondary phases could dominate the mechanical response if the alloy is not single-phase BCC.

contradictions.description: The intervention claims to isolate lattice-distortion effects, but the alloy and tungsten differ simultaneously in composition, processing route, grain structure, grain-boundary character, and possible segregation. The uncertainty field explicitly acknowledges some of these alternative causes, so the proposed comparison cannot by itself isolate lattice distortion.
